The tin whistle is a simple six-hole wooden wind instrument of the duct flute family, the same class as the recorder and the Native American flute; it sounds through a duct, and the player uses six-hole fingering close to that of the traditional six-hole flute. It is common in Celtic music and Irish traditional music, and is also used in English, Scottish and American traditional music, mostly for domestic or folk playing. Because the key is fixed, semitones are hard to play, so players usually pick a whistle in a particular key for each piece, most often D and C. Its Hornbostel–Sachs number is 421.221.12.
